items.title: U.S. says it shot down Iranian missiles targeting troops in Middle East - The Washington Post
items.summary: # U.S. says it shot down Iranian missiles targeting troops in Middle East. The attempted attack risks upending a period of relative calm as President Donald Trump sought to advance peace negotiations. Pro-government demonstrators chant at a gathering in Tehran on Tuesday. The U.S. military said Tuesday that its forces in the Middle East intercepted multiple ballistic missiles that Iran had fired at American personnel there, potentially upending a pause in military operations that President Donald Trump had sought in a bid to advance stalled peace negotiations. items.title: Iran launches 'attempted surprise attack' on US forces in Middle East - BBC
items.summary: # Iran launches 'attempted surprise attack' on US forces in Middle East. Iran has launched "multiple" ballistic missiles in an "attempted surprise attack" on American forces in the Middle East, the US military says, shattering a lull in the fighting. The attack occurred at 17:45 EDT (21:45 GMT) on Tuesday, and all missiles were "successfully intercepted", said US Central Command, without specifying the locations of any targets. The alleged assault occurred during a break in hostilities between the two countries, which was designed to bring negotiators back to the table. US President Donald Trump spoke on Monday of "very friendly negotiations" with Iran, after the two sides had not exchanged strikes for a third straight day. But he had also cautioned that the US could "go back to doing what we were doing" before the break in hostilities. ## As the US pauses the war with Iran, is Trump really running out of weapons?

items.title: US, Saudis attack Iran-backed groups in Iraq, threatening to intensify conflict - Reuters
items.summary: ## Browse World. DUBAI/CAIRO, July 29 (Reuters) - The U.S. and Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq on Wednesday, saying they were responsible for drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities, prompting Iran to warn ​that blaming it for such attacks was a "major miscalculation". The strikes on targets inside Iraq come as Oman proposed a new regional deal aimed at resolving the conflict over ‌the critical Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flowed before the war. The U.S.-Saudi strikes in eastern Iraq occurred just hours after the U.S. military said its ​air defences had averted a surprise Iranian attack on U.S. troops in the region. In an effort ​to resolve the conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, ​Oman has presented Iran with a plan ⁠backed by Gulf states to manage the waterway that would include collecting voluntary fees from ships, a Gulf source and a Western diplomat told Reuters on Tuesday.

items.title: Iran launches surprise ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces in the Middle East - CNBC
items.summary: # Iran launches surprise ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces in the Middle East. * Iran launches a "surprise attack" on U.S. forces in the Middle East. * The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported "suspicious activity," in the Red Sea in a post on X. Iran targeted American forces in the Middle East with ballistic missiles late Tuesday stateside, U.S. Central Command said, raising tensions in the region again after the warring sides had briefly halted hostilities. Centcom in a post on X said that the attack originated from Iran, but all missiles were intercepted. "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on U.S. forces based in the Middle East.". In a subsequent statement posted on X, Centcom said U.S. and Saudi forces struck "multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites" in eastern Iraq Tuesday stateside, retaliating against more than 30 drone attacks in the past three days by "Iran-aligned terrorists.". Separately, the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported "suspicious activity," in the Red Sea in a post on X.

items.title: Trump signals diplomacy with Iran as Hormuz talks continue - World Oil
items.summary: (Bloomberg) – U.S. President Donald Trump said he’d prefer to avoid another escalation in the war with Iran and urged Tehran to make a deal, laying the ground for further diplomacy after both sides paused tit-for-tat strikes. His comments came four days after the U.S. ended roughly two weeks of strikes on the Islamic Republic following a breakdown in peace negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran in turn pausing retaliatory fire on Gulf states. A deal to get ships moving through the waterway more frequently would enable the Islamic Republic and the U.S. to resume formal negotiations about Tehran’s nuclear program and permanently end their war, the people said. Netanyahu has said he plans to press the U.S. leader on keeping a “constant watch” on Iran’s nuclear program, one of many issues now in limbo following the breakdown of an interim peace deal from mid-June.
